column1: # What CI is allowed to cost, and why.
# Format: constant<TAB>value    (seconds, decimal, no units in the value)
# Beside check-owners.tsv because it is the same kind of fact: that table says
# where CI runs a check, this one says how long CI may take to run them all.
# Both are declared here and read out of here, never restated in a workflow.
# Readers: scripts/derive-shards.py, which picks the shard count that fits the
# budget and refuses a file that declares none, and verify.sh's
# `report_wall_clock`, which prints every run against it. NOTHING FAILS A RUN
# ON THESE NUMBERS. A slow gate is not a wrong gate, and a budget that can fail
# a build is a budget somebody raises rather than meets. What they buy is that
# the overrun is in the log of the run that caused it.
# --- the budget ---
# A seat that waits on CI comes back to a COLD PREFIX if the wait outlasts its
# provider's prompt-cache TTL, and then pays the whole prefill again at cold
# rates. The TTL is ~30 minutes on first-party Anthropic and ~5 minutes on
# Bedrock, so five minutes is the shortest any seat on this repository runs on
# and is therefore the ceiling: past it, somebody is paying for the runners not
# being tuned. It is a WALL CLOCK, not a sum of runner-minutes -- those are
# unbilled on this repository and are the currency this budget spends.
# Ruled on #87 (2026-09-19), against a run that took 7m27s.
wall_clock_seconds
# --- what the run costs that is not the selftest itself ---
# A selftest shard's `./verify.sh --selftest --shard` step is not the whole
# run. Around it sit the checkout, `cargo --version` resolving the pinned
# toolchain, apt-get for bubblewrap, the census upload, the run's own admission
# of each job, and the `gate` job, which cannot start until the last shard
# finishes. All of that comes off the budget BEFORE the faults are packed: the
# count derive-shards.py picks is the one whose slowest shard's STEP fits in
# `wall_clock_seconds` minus this.
# MEASURED, and measured on the runner, which is the one number in this file a
# local harvest cannot produce. From run 35415319419 (PR #86, eight shards, all
# green), by the job and step timestamps the Actions API reports:
#   run created 02:19:41Z, `gate` finished 02:27:08Z        447s end to end
#   slowest selftest step (shard 2)  02:20:02 -> 02:26:56   414s
#   everything that is not that step                         33s
#   of which, per shard: checkout + toolchain + apt + sysctl  19-24s
#                        census upload + post-checkout         2-4s
#   and once per run:    admission, then the `gate` job        ~11s
# One shard in that run (shard 3) was admitted 36s after its siblings, which no
# amount of packing recovers and which grows with the shard count. 60 is
# therefore above the 33s measured and below the 77s a maximally unlucky
# admission would cost. It errs HIGH on purpose: a too-large overhead buys more
# shards than strictly needed, and runner-minutes are unbilled here, while a
# too-small one buys a count that does not fit and the budget is missed.
# Re-measure it when the steps around the selftest change.
runner_overhead_seconds
# --- the ceiling on the shard count ---
# The account runs 20 concurrent jobs. Past that a shard does not start until
# something finishes, so the wall clock stops falling and starts queueing, and
# a packer that did not know it would keep splitting.
# 20, the real number, not a number shaded down to leave headroom for
# `verify.yml`'s diet, pages and repo jobs: reserving margin here is a second
# budget nobody declared, competing with the one this file exists to be. If
# twenty does not get the slowest shard under `wall_clock_seconds`, that is an
# UNMET BUDGET, and an unmet budget is disclosed, not faked by a shard count
# the account cannot actually run concurrently -- `report_wall_clock` prints
# the achieved wall-clock against this budget on every run, and
# `derive-shards.py`'s own emitted header says so when the ceiling is what it
# packed against. The next lever past shard count -- per-shard build time --
# is its own item, outside #87's scope by #87's own text.
max_shards
